newsitem.title: FRANCE: Gunmen kill four, kidnap six girls in Algeria - paper.
newsitem.headline: Gunmen kill four, kidnap six girls in Algeria - paper.

text.p: Suspected Moslem rebels killed four people and kidnapped six girls, all from one family, in a night-time attack south of Algiers, an Algerian newspaper said on Sunday.
El Watan daily said the gunmen broke into the family home in the centre of Larba, 25 km (15 miles) from the capital, killed the four and forced the girls, aged 13 to 28, to go with them.
Neighbours, fearing they might be attacked, did nothing to alert the security forces during the raid last Wednesday night, the newspaper said.

EL Watan blamed the attack on Moslem guerrillas who have carried out numerous attacks on homes and villages with the apparent aim of kidnapping young women to serve as "temporary brides" for their men in the bush.
Few of the girls are ever reported to return safely.
More than 200 civilians have been reported killed in Algeria in the four weeks since the June 5 general election in which moderate Islamists won 103 seats in the 380-member National Assembly.
President Liamine Zeroual, who is striving to pacify the country from a five and a half years of violence, barred radical Islamists from fielding candidates in the poll.
More than 60,000 people have died in Algeria since 1992 when the authorities cancelled a general election in which radical Islamists had taken a commanding lead.
